title: Orientation and incidence numbers on a cell complex
body_html:
Orientation and incidence numbers

For a locally finite regular CW complex $X$ we fix a family of incidence numbers

$$[E : F] \in \mathbb{Z}, \qquad E, F \in [\![X]\!],$$

supported on codim-1 face pairs and satisfying

  • $[E : F] = 0$ whenever $E \not\preceq F$;
  • $[E : F] = 0$ whenever $\dim F \neq \dim E + 1$;
  • the chain-complex axiom $\partial^2 = 0$: for any pair $D, F$ with $\dim F = \dim D + 2$,

$$\sum_{E \in [\![X]\!]} [D : E] \cdot [E : F] = 0.$$

Such a family is called an orientation of $X$.

Regularity

An orientation is regular if $[E : F] \in \{+1, -1\}$ whenever $E \preceq F$ and $\dim F = \dim E + 1$. Combinatorially this matches the topological condition that each attaching map is an embedding onto its image; every regular CW complex admits a regular orientation.

$G$-equivariance

When a group $G$ acts cellularly on $X$, an orientation is $G$-equivariant when

$$[g \cdot E : g \cdot F] = [E : F], \qquad g \in G, \ E, F \in [\![X]\!].$$

Equivariance is the appropriate condition for connected acting groups (no sign character); disconnected acting groups may act through a sign character on $\mathbb{Z}$, but the paper's setting is connected.

Downstream use

The orientation feeds into the boundary of the cellular chain complex of a cosheaf: see [[node:representations.chain_complex_C_dot]].
